title: Medi Assist Healthcare Services Ltd - 544088 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Medi Assist FY26: total income up 23.6% to INR923.2 crore, operating EBITDA margin 19.3%, company turned debt-free in Jan 2026.
summary.overview: FY26 showed strong top-line growth with total income of INR923.2 crore (up 23.6% YoY) and operating income of INR904.8 crore (up 25.1%). Operating EBITDA reached INR174.6 crore at a 19.3% margin, with quarterly margin expanding from 17.1% in Q2 to 18.6% in Q3 and 19.9% in Q4. Reported PAT was INR89.3 crore, while adjusted PAT was INR68.8 crore after exceptional items. The group became debt-free in January 2026, and Paramount TPA operations were transferred into Medi Assist TPA effective 1 February 2026.

segments.name: Group
segments.commentary: Revenue INR629.1 crore, about 69.5% of total, up 25.3% YoY. Group premium under administration above INR23,000 crore (up 25.6%), with retention of 93.2%, below the historical 94%+.

segments.name: Retail (TPA model)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR95.5 crore, about 10.6% of total, up 10.9% YoY. TPA-model retail premium INR2,818 crore (up 4.2%); market share 5%, slightly lower YoY. Premiums on MAtrix for private insurers exceed INR18,000 crore (about 32% of industry retail premium).

segments.name: Government
segments.commentary: Revenue INR113.6 crore, about 12.6% of total, up 42.6% YoY. Work spans 13 states and 3 union territories.

segments.name: International Benefits Administration
segments.commentary: Revenue INR41.1 crore, about 4.5% of total, up 11.9% YoY. Management said there is little or no exposure to the Middle East; a group-segment slowdown was seen from IT-ITES headcount cuts.

segments.name: Technology SaaS
segments.commentary: Revenue INR21.7 crore, about 2.5% of total, up 91.9% YoY. Current revenue comes only from the core SaaS claims platform (MAtrix), with no AI or outcome-based features yet billed.

guidance_outlook: Paramount TPA integration: over 50% of Paramount Health Services' claims volume migrated to MAtrix; full migration to primary processing engine expected before Q2 FY27. Management tracks to synergies within 1-2 quarters from now, against a 4-5 quarter norm.
Technology and international revenue growth expected to continue at similar rates to FY26 or better, per management.
Core business expected to match or beat industry growth; management cited 8-10% blended same-store group growth currently.
Management gave a directional aspiration (explicitly not guidance) that technology margins could be 1.5-2x the traditional TPA business as non-headcount yield is captured.
Exceptional items (including insurance claims and disallowed claims) remain open and will be carried each quarter until resolved.
capex_capacity: Nearly one million claims processed per month on AI-powered platforms, per management.
MAven Guard fraud detection prevented over INR540 crore of frauds in FY26; network discounts delivered over INR1,300 crore last year.
Raksha Prime enabled over 322,000 patients to walk out before bills were generated, across 6,000 hospitals in FY26.
Nearly one-third of headcount is contractually obligated to public-health schemes, serving 27 crore members.
AI capabilities can now be deployed on top of legacy or third-party claims platforms, not only on MAtrix.
demand_pricing: Total premium under management INR25,923 crore as of 31 March 2026, up 22.8%; market share of group plus retail in total health premium 20.7%, up 115 bps.
Group market share up 340 bps to 33.7%; group premium grew 25.6% including Paramount.
Group yields are compressing partly because of low-ticket-size benefit add-ons that are not fully priced; management says effort-to-remuneration metrics remain healthy.
Group same-store growth has slowed from about 25% post-COVID to an estimated 8-10% blended; over INR2,000 crore of new group premium added organically in FY26.
IT-ITES headcount reductions are the main drag on group lives; other sectors such as oil and gas and chemicals are growing.
Management views outcome-based pricing as the eventual direction for AI-led services; no fixed-price AI contracts exist today.
Management estimated the Indian health premium administered by TPAs at roughly 50% of the market, with the other 50% in areas like personal accident outside TPA scope.

qa_highlights.question: How can the company build dominance in retail given its strength in group?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described retail as a hybrid model: TPA-led for high-frequency outpatient products and technology plug-ins for insurers' own front ends, with the premium under MAtrix reported separately.

qa_highlights.question: How can investors track earnings on the technology business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose a take rate. It offered a directional aspiration of 1.5-2x traditional TPA margins, stating this was not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is group retention (93.2%) below last year and what about PSU allocations?
qa_highlights.answer: Retention dipped due to deliberate quality-of-revenue decisions and operational transition; management expects a return to slightly higher retention. PSU allocations are driven by insurer cycles and are outside the company's control.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Bima Sugam on the business over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect disruption, arguing claims adjudication, network, and fraud control remain needed; it cited integration with NHCX and work in 13 states and 3 UTs contributing over INR113 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How far can AI automate claims, and could take rates fall from around 3.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most claims processing is rule-driven and targets 70-80% automation; it declined to forecast yield changes, attributing yield compression to lower-ticket benefit products.

qa_highlights.question: Paramount integration timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said integration is 3 quarters in with Q4 margins up about 130 bps QoQ, and expects synergies within 1-2 more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to the Middle East conflict and the exceptional item recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: No material Middle East exposure; the international slowdown was limited to group, with some operational challenges on seafarer cover. Exceptional items remain open and are disclosed in the notes.

risks_watch: Group same-store growth slowing (about 8-10% blended) with IT-ITES headcount cuts; watch lives growth in non-IT sectors.
Group retention at 93.2%, below the historical 94%+; watch for recovery in Q1 FY27.
Yield compression from low-ticket benefit products; management did not give a forward view on take rate.
Paramount migration to MAtrix before Q2 FY27 and synergy delivery in 1-2 quarters.
Regulatory and policy risk from Bima Sugam and the National Health Claims Exchange; management sees no near-term disruption.
Retail TPA-model premium growth of only 4.2% and market share slipping to 5%.
Technology revenue remains about 2.5% of total; watch disclosed growth of AI modules and first outcome-based contracts.
Open exceptional items and insurance claims on disallowed items continue into subsequent quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, margins, and technology, with clear statements on Paramount integration timing. Evasive or non-committal on yield trajectory, take rate, and specific guidance, which management repeatedly labelled as not guidance. Cautious on group growth given IT-ITES headcount cuts.
key_quotes: Becoming debt-free and net cash positive strengthens our ability to invest in the future, while our AI-powered platforms are now operating at unprecedented scale, processing nearly 1 million claims every month with industry-leading automation and fraud detection.
We're 3 quarters down. And I think our quarterly margins in Q4 also went up by another 130 bps compared to Q3.
Much as we would like to say AI will automate a claim. What we need AI for right now urgently in the country is to make sure inputs are good enough for the rule engines.
